subject: general
question: In Δ ABC, BD ⊥ AC at D and ∠DBC = 54º. E is a point on BC such that ∠CAE= 34º. What is the measure of ∠AEB?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **ΔBDC**, **∠BDC = 90º** and **∠DBC = 54º**. ∴ **∠C = 180º − (90º + 54º) = 36º**.

In **ΔAEC**, **∠AEB** is the **Exterior Angle** at vertex **E**.

**∠AEB = ∠EAC + ∠C**

⇒ **∠AEB = 34º + 36º = 70º**.

**∴ The correct answer is 70º.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **BD ⊥ AC**, **∠DBC = 54º**, **∠CAE = 34º**.

**Formula Used:** Sum of angles in a triangle is **180º**; **Exterior Angle Theorem**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dcfbdad23948648bbbf64db45e07d8b89263b500e181b30ba60b935f3ff52619.png] 

Step 1: Consider **ΔBDC**.

⇒ **∠BDC = 90º** (Since **BD ⊥ AC**)

⇒ **∠DBC + ∠BCD + ∠BDC = 180º**

⇒ **54º + ∠C + 90º = 180º**

⇒ **∠C = 180º − 144º = 36º**

Step 2: Consider **ΔAEC**.

⇒ **∠CAE = 34º** (Given)

⇒ **∠AEB** is the **Exterior Angle** for **ΔAEC** at vertex **E**.

⇒ **∠AEB = ∠EAC + ∠ACE**

⇒ **∠AEB = 34º + 36º = 70º**.

**∴ The correct answer is 70º.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

The measure of an **Exterior Angle** of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two **Remote Interior Angles**.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all **Interior Angles** of any triangle is always **180º**.

Right-Angled Triangle Property

In a **Right-Angled Triangle**, the two **Acute Angles** are always **Complementary** (their sum is **90º**).</p
